title: Cohorted deploy wave mapping and stakeholder comms protocol
creator: Riley Thompson
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable, SLO-driven approach for mapping deploy cohorts (waves) across runtime, console, and API surfaces, plus a formalized stakeholder communication protocol and ownership roster for each wave. This ticket standardizes cohort sizing, regional and tier gating, preflight checks, and automatic calendar signals so Product, Eng, Design, and Support can coordinate launches with predictable capacity hedges and clear rollback criteria.

Scope:
- Wave definition templates (size, % traffic, duration, rollback thresholds) for canaries, early adopter cohorts, and general availability.
- Mapping of waves to capacity lanes (hosted/dedicated/private) and region-specific fallback plans.
- SLO-driven gating rules that block or advance waves based on latency/error budgets from runtime and console dashboards.
- Stakeholder comms protocol (preflight, go/no-go, mid-window cadence, incident escalation) with named role responsibilities and a timeboxed operations window.
- Owner roster automation: link wave windows to on-call rotations and cross-team owners; include secondary contacts.
- Integration points: CI/CD release pipeline signals, Console launch calendar, and Launch Ops Slack channel hooks.

Out of scope: model-level rollout specifics and per-customer reserved capacity contracts (handled in Dedicated capacity playbooks).
acceptance_criteria: Wave template artifacts created and stored in Confluence with example parameters for small (5%), medium (20%), and large (100%) cohorts
Gating rules documented and implemented as checklist items in the Console launch calendar (PASS/FAIL conditions linked to runtime latency and error dashboards)
Owner roster automation wireframe and a working demo that assigns primary/secondary owners from on-call schedules
Comms protocol has approved templates for preflight, go/no-go, mid-window updates, and rollback announcements
Two simulated launches executed (one cross-surface canary and one GA wave) with post-mortem showing correct enforcement of gates and comms flow
notes: Trade-off: tighter SLO gates reduce blast radius but increase rollbacks and manual intervention. We favor automated soft-gates (warning) + hard-gates for critical metrics (error-rate, 99th latency).
Decision so far: default cohort sizes will be conservative (5% canary -> 25% ramp -> flush) for runtime changes that touch kernel scheduling; console-only UI changes may use larger initial cohorts.
Fallback policy: when cross-region capacity is constrained, automatically divert to a compatible model variant or lower-tier instance family (prefers lower-latency region first).
Design review requested: DES team to provide banner copy and in-console signal indicators for active wave windows by 2026-02-10 (blocked currently on DES-220 backlog).

risks: If SLO gates are too aggressive we will see more rollbacks and increased manual toil; mitigation: add warning windows and human-in-the-loop gating for non-critical metrics.
Design blockers (DES-220) may reduce visibility into active wave state for pilot — mitigation: use Slack + Console page updates and ensure Support has pre-built FAQ.
Cross-surface dependencies (runtime + console + API) increase coordination complexity; mitigation: require checklist sign-off from each surface owner before advancing wave.
open_questions: Should enterprise P1 customers be excluded from automated ramp and instead handled via scheduled Reserved Capacity cutover?
Do we need a dedicated 'rollback burst' capacity lane in Dedicated to absorb traffic during rollbacks?
What is the acceptable SLA for publishing mid-window updates to external customers (e.g., 15 minutes vs 60 minutes)?
